newsitem.title: USA: Bomb damages California bank, another is disarmed.
newsitem.headline: Bomb damages California bank, another is disarmed.

text.p: An explosion damaged a bank early on Sunday, hours after a bomb containing 30 sticks of dynamite was found and dismantled outside a public library in the same California town, authorities said.
Police in Vallejo, located about 35 miles (53 km) northeast of San Francisco, said an explosion occurred outside a Wells Fargo Bank branch just before 3 a.m. local time (1100 GMT)on Sunday.
The device caused extensive damage to automated teller machines on the east side of the building. No injuries were reported and no money was taken from the cash machines.
Hours earlier, Vallejo police said a large bomb was found leaning against the wall of a downtown public library that houses a police evidence room in its basement.
Police said they responded to the scene late on Saturday afternoon. The area was evacuated as a bomb disposal team dismantled the device, police said.

The library bomb was found by two children, who were playing with the wiring before they realised it could be an explosive device. Police said the bomb contained at least 30 sticks of dynamite and was powerful enough to have caused extensive damage and many injuries in the area.
Vallejo police said they had no leads.

Local, state and federal authorities said they were working jointly on the investigation, collecting evidence from the scenes and trying to determine if there are similarities between the two devices.
